title: The Physicist Who Accidentally Froze Time in a Crystal
hook: A researcher trapped a light pulse inside a crystal for 60 seconds—then watched it emerge as a perfect ghost of itself.
why_this_can_go_viral: Sounds like magic but is real physics; the 'ghost image' hook creates a mental puzzle viewers want solved.

title: The Biolab That Bred Mosquitoes That Only Bite Men
hook: A genetic modification experiment targeted male pheromones—and the mosquitoes learned to ignore women entirely.
why_this_can_go_viral: Sex-specific horror triggers personal relevance; the 'why' behind the targeting feels sinister and unexplainable.

title: The Neuroscientist Who Erased a Rat's Fear—and It Walked Into a Trap
hook: By zapping a single synapse, a researcher removed a rodent's lifelong terror of cats—with deadly consequences.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visceral animal horror combined with 'what if it happened to humans' fear makes it an instant anxiety hook.

title: The Chemistry Disaster Where a Scientist Boiled Acid in a Closed Room—and Dissolved His Lungs
hook: A 1972 lab mistake created hydrofluoric acid vapor so concentrated that a researcher's lungs turned to gel in minutes.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme gore and 'worst way to die' psychology; body horror is the highest engagement category in science short-form.

title: The Scientific Fraud Who Faked a 'Telepathy' Machine—and Got a Nobel Nomination
hook: A respected physicist convinced the world he built a machine that transmitted thoughts—until a student discovered the wire.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes how easily institutions are fooled; 'Nobel nomination for a hoax' is a high-status betrayal story.

title: The Lab Catastrophe Where a Scientist Was Sprayed With Liquid Nitrogen—and Shattered His Arm
hook: A cryogenic tank valve failed, spraying -196°C liquid directly onto a researcher's forearm—which broke off like glass.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme rarity and visceral imagery; 'shattered like glass' is a phrase that mentally replays.

title: The Biolab That Engineered a Glowing Rabbit—and It Never Stopped Glowing
hook: A 2000 experiment spliced jellyfish DNA into a rabbit embryo—and the offspring glowed green for life, even in the dark.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual spectacle with a creepy 'never stopped' twist; feels like a sci-fi movie premise.

title: The Scientific Fraud Who Faked a 'Crystal That Heals Cancer'—and Patients Stopped Chemo
hook: A dim-witted entrepreneur sold quartz crystals as 'radiation neutralizers'—and cancer patients died believing in magic rocks.
why_this_can_go_viral: Outrage at preventable deaths plus the 'dumb villain' angle makes it emotionally charged and shareable.

title: The Lab Catastrophe Where a Gamma Source Was Dropped—and a Technician's Hand Died in Hours
hook: In 1999, a sealed cesium-137 capsule fell off a conveyor belt; the man who picked it up lost his hand to radiation necrosis within a day.
why_this_can_go_viral: The rapid decay of living tissue is pure body horror; 'hand died in hours' is a stunning fact.

title: The Quantum Paradox Where a Particle Spin Determined Its Own Measurement History
hook: In a delayed-choice quantum eraser setup, the spin of a particle after detection retroactively decided which path it 'took' before the measurement.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'future controls the past' hook breaks intuitive causality; high curiosity gap drives rewatches.

title: The Forbidden Experiment Where a Scientist Injected Himself with His Own Blood—and Died of Allergic Shock
hook: In 1901, a researcher trying to prove self-immunity injected his own blood intravenously. His body attacked itself within minutes.
why_this_can_go_viral: The irony of 'proving immunity by dying' is dark humor; personal experimentation horror resonates.

title: The Neuroscientist Who Made a Blind Man See—Using a Camera Attached to His Tongue
hook: A brain plasticity experiment rerouted visual data through the tongue's nerves—and a blind subject could recognize faces in days.
why_this_can_go_viral: Sounds like a superpower; the 'tongue sees' hook is bizarre enough to make anyone click.

title: The Chemistry Disaster That Created a Green Glow—and the Scientist's Teeth Glowed for Months
hook: A 1940s radium spill in a lab left a chemist's teeth, bones, and urine glowing green for over a year—he died of bone cancer.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ghastly visual of a glowing, dying man; 'teeth glowed for months' is unforgettable and grotesque.

title: The Scientific Fraud Who Faked a 'Quantum Healing' Machine—and Opened 200 Clinics
hook: A con artist sold $50,000 'quantum resonance' boxes that claimed to cure any disease—until a patient opened one and found a light bulb inside.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes how easily people are scammed; the 'light bulb' reveal is a perfect punchline that drives shares.

title: The Biolab That Created a 'Suicide Gene'—and It Spread to Wild Bacteria
hook: A genetically engineered 'kill switch' escaped a containment lab and jumped into wild bacteria, making them self-destruct—but not before spreading.
why_this_can_go_viral: Real-life biohazard thriller; the idea of uncontrollable self-destruction in nature is terrifying and fascinating.

title: The Physicist Who Found That Time Flows Backward Inside a Black Hole—and Published It
hook: A 2023 theoretical paper argued that inside a black hole's event horizon, the arrow of time reverses—and everything untangles.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'time reversal' concept is mind-bending and easy to visualize; 'published it' adds credibility.

title: The Lab Catastrophe Where a Scientist Was Injected with Prion-Infected Brain Tissue—and Lived for Decades
hook: In 1978, a researcher accidentally stabbed herself with a needle containing Creutzfeldt-Jakob brain extract—she didn't die until 2016.
why_this_can_go_viral: The decades-long countdown to death is a slow-burn horror story; prion diseases are famously terrifying.

title: The Quantum Paradox Where a Computer Calculated with Particles That Didn't Exist
hook: A quantum algorithm ran on 'virtual' qubits that were never physically present—yet it output the correct answer.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that something can compute using 'nothing' defies logic; high confusion drives engagement.
